BURGOS Sangguniang Bayan Secretary Sanggunian Bayan of Jose Abad Santos, Davao Occidental Door 9, Ground Floor, Municipal Hall, Malita, Davao Occidental Dear Ms. Burgos: s. 202 This has reference to your letter dated 26 October 2018 requesting for the Department's opinion on the Sanggunian Bayan's withdrawal of a previously granted Mayor's authority to contract a loan with Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) in the amount of P 100,000,000.00 and all previously granted authority relative thereto. Such withdrawal is by way of the following resolution and ordinance: 1. Resolution No. 069, S. 2018, enacted on October 2, 2018, re.•A RESOLUTION WITHDRA WING THE AUTHORITY GRANTED TO HON. JAMES' Y JOYCE, MUNICIPAL MA YOR, TO CONTRACT LOAN WITH THE L4ND BANK OF THE PHILIPPPINES IN THE AMOUNT OF ONE HUNDRED MILLION PESOS 00) AND ALL PREVIOUSL Y GRANTED A UTHORITY RELA TIVE THERETO; and 2. Ordinance No. 04, S. 2018, enacted on the same date, re: AN ORDINANCE WITHDRA WING THE AUTHORITY GRANTED TO HON. JAMES Y. JOYCE, MUNICIPAL MA YOR, TO CONTRACTLOAN WITH THE LAND BANK OF THE PHILIPINES IN THE AMOUNT OF ONE HUNDRED MILLION PESOS AND REPEALING ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS REIM TIVE THERETO In connection thereto, posed for this Department's opinion are the herein below quoted queries: 1. "Can the SB withdraw the authority to the Mayor in spite of the facts that the same SB membership knew that the Mayor had already signed the contract being that the signed contract (with Annex "A " to the Loan Agreement) were furnished back to the SB for ratification and being ratified by the same SB membership? Ifthe answer

is yes, can the SB withdraw that authority based on the grounds enumerated in the resolution/ordinance? 2. Whether or not the resolution to withdraw authority to LCE to contract loan need be submitted to the LCE for appropriate action and can this resolution override the previously approved ordinance? 3. Which ordinance between that of granting authority and that of withdrawing authority to contract loan should or may the LCE rely upon as basis of his executive actions?" At the outset, the assailed Sanggunian Resolution and Ordinance have undergone the legislative process for its passage in accordance with R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991". By said fact, they are embraced with presumptive validity unless declared otherwise by competent authority. Thus, any issue or question as to its substantive validity and enforceability must not be threshed out before this Department. In any similar case where no resolution/ordinance has yet been enacted, the Department stands consistent with DILG Opinion No. 93, series of 2003, that once the authority has been given and the contract or agreement has already been entered into and perfected, the Sanggunian is not anymore at liberty to withdraw its Resolution authorizing the Mayor to enter into a contract as it would clearly impair and prejudice the vested right of the people, who is the real contracting party, conferred upon the perfection thereof. To date, the Department finds no cogent reason to depart from the aforementioned opinion. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Thank you. cc Legal/84A Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary for Local Government DIR.ALEX C. ROLDAN, CESO V DILG Region X1
